task_completion.description: Set the observer location to Paranal Observatory, Chile.
task_completion.visual_evidence: Location settings or status bar showing 'Paranal', 'Chile', or coordinates near 24.6° S, 70.4° W.

task_completion.description: Set the simulation time to December 21, 2020, at approximately 18:00 UTC.
task_completion.visual_evidence: Date/Time display showing 2020-12-21 and a time near 18:00:00 UTC (or equivalent local time).

task_completion.description: Navigate the view to the region containing Jupiter and Saturn.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The labels or icons for Jupiter and Saturn appearing in the field of view.

task_completion.description: Center the view on the conjunction point between the two planets.
task_completion.visual_evidence: Jupiter and Saturn positioned near the center of the screen, often indicated by a selection reticle or crosshair.

task_completion.description: Adjust the field of view (zoom) so that both planets and their moons are clearly visible simultaneously.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A high-magnification view where Jupiter's disk/moons (e.g., Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto) and Saturn's disk/moons (e.g., Titan) are visible in the same frame.

integrity.visual_evidence: Mouse cursor movements, menu clicks, or dialog boxes visible in screenshots.

integrity.description: The agent interacted with the live simulation environment.
integrity.visual_evidence: Changes in the UI state, such as time ticking or FOV values changing, across consecutive screenshots.

integrity.description: The agent used the search or navigation tools within the app to find the planets.
integrity.visual_evidence: Search bar entries for 'Jupiter' or 'Saturn' or manual slewing visible in the trajectory.

privileged_info_for_vlm: On 2020-12-21 at 18:00 UTC, Jupiter and Saturn were at a Great Conjunction with a very close separation of approximately 6.1 arcminutes. Jupiter's coordinates: RA ~20h 18m, Dec ~-20.5°. Saturn's coordinates: RA ~20h 18m, Dec ~-20.4°. Jupiter is brighter (mag -1.97) than Saturn (mag 0.63). At this zoom level, the Galilean moons of Jupiter and Titan of Saturn should be visible in a single field of view of roughly 0.2 to 0.5 degrees.
